qa.question: Should the Mount Pleasant fleet be raised from 672 MW to the permit's 722.5 MW?
qa.finding: GEM carries 146 + 39 + 39 engines at 3 MW each, 672 MW. The DNR preliminary determination for permit 25-MIN-113 lists 244 engines that sum to 722.5 MW, and the Aug 2026 application adds 6 half-megawatt and 9 one-megawatt Caterpillar units for Area 2.
qa.recommendation: Leave GEM's three rows as they are for now. Ask the project manager whether the one-megawatt, half-megawatt and Clarke fire pump units (which GEM does not carry) should be added as extra rows.
qa.note:
Where to look:
- Preliminary determination at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1262690, Source Description table. It lists Cummins C3000 D6e at 'up to 3,213' kW for each of 39 + 39 + 146 core engines, plus smaller Cummins 500DFEK, 1000DQFAD and Clarke fire pump units.
- Application at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1287957, Section 1.2 and Table 1, and Appendix B table 'Mount Pleasant Area Designations'. It lists Area 2 as 146 three-megawatt units, 9 one-megawatt units and 9 half-megawatt units.
- 39 x 3.213 MW is 125.3 MW against 117 MW in GEM. The permit figure is the largest rating allowed, so I made no change.
- The application also names Area East (136 acres) and a 150-acre parcel Microsoft is acquiring, which would be further fleets. Amalia Llano's note and the Mount Pleasant village agendas were not read separately.

qa.question: Is 3 MW or 3.213 MW the right capacity per core engine at Mount Pleasant?
qa.finding: The permit table gives 3,213 kW for each Cummins C3000 D6e. GEM uses 3 MW.
qa.recommendation: Keep 3 MW unless the manual says to use the permit's maximum rating; if it does, change Capacity Per Engine to 3.213 and recompute unit capacity.
qa.note: Open https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1262690 and the Source Description table, column 'Capacity (kW)': '≤ 3,213' for Cummins C3000 D6e. No document I found gives the nameplate electrical rating directly.
